clue.text: Sent a message about Slovenian tourist destination

blocks.note: CA, short for circa, means about
Bled is a lakeside resort in Slovenia

explanation.surface: Someone on holiday wires home about a pretty Slovenian lake town.
explanation.definitionFit: To cable is to send a telegram, so the past tense matches a message having been sent.

clue.text: Charlie, on French river, making soup

blocks.note: Charlie is the radio alphabet word for C
taken as written
the Somme is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie, beside a river in France, is cooking soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear broth, a kind of soup.

clue.text: Lacking sharpness, trombone, say, in club?

blocks.note: something without an edge or point is blunt
a trombone is an example of a musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone at a club night complains that a trombone player sounds dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'club' a nightclub where a band plays; it is really a cudgel, the classic weapon of the police report.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is a heavy stick, and 'blunt instrument' is the stock phrase for such an unedged weapon.

clue.text: Girl from Israeli port brought over around one

indicators.note: around tells us one word wraps about another piece
brought over suggests turning something over, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: Acre is a port city in northern Israel
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl is fetched from an Israeli harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Put I inside ACRE to get ACIRE, then turn it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Desert that woman? On the contrary

blocks.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to abandon a woman, and gets a contradicting reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a sandy noun but is the verb rat, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather, used as an interjection, contradicts or corrects what was just said, much like 'on the contrary'.

clue.text: Social worker, woman, having short chat before the baby's born

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word for chat loses its last letter

blocks.note: ants are social insects and the workers are the ones that labour
Ena is a woman's name
to talk is to chat

explanation.surface: A social worker and a woman have a quick chat before the birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a council employee, but it is the insect that lives in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal means relating to the period of pregnancy, the time before a birth.

clue.text: Struck senior teacher - possible punishment to get prominent media attention

blocks.note: to strike is to hit
the head teacher runs a school
lines are a school punishment of writing out a sentence many times

explanation.surface: A pupil who hit the headmaster, facing punishment, ends up in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines are a British school penalty: copying out a sentence over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the headlines is an idiom for becoming front-page news.

clue.text: Meal for old man, among others

indicators.note: among places one thing in the middle of a group, so one word sits inside another

blocks.note: the rest are the others
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dinner is laid on for Dad along with everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal or literary word for a meal.

clue.text: Roofing material which church required

blocks.note: that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A note on what the village church needed for its roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reed laid as roof covering, so it is a material for roofs.

clue.text: A squalid property surrounding yard provides sanctuary

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written
a slum is run-down, squalid housing
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A grim tenement with a yard offers shelter to someone in need.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or refuge given to someone fleeing danger, the same idea as sanctuary.

clue.text: Brings up in houses built across river

indicators.note: something built is put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order
across means spanning, so the rearranged letters stretch over one more

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone raises a family in homes built on both banks of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish a child is to feed and rear it, which is to bring it up.

clue.text: Count's child at university

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: A nobleman's young child is now studying at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count's' looks like a title with a possessive; it is the verb plus 's for 'is'. Being up means in residence at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is a phrasal verb for adding numbers together, which is to count.

clue.text: Unfashionable shed one rejected

blocks.note: something out of fashion is out
a snake casts, or sheds, its skin

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned garden shed has been thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut but is the past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a person cast out by society, someone rejected.

clue.text: Starts to avoid key meals

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: to launch something is to start it
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to skip the main meals of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: A musical key is one of the letters A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunches are midday meals, so the plural noun matches meals.

clue.text: Groom's award in sport?

blocks.note: surface reading: the prize given to the best player in a game
setter's reading: a match is also a marriage, and the groom is its man

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for the best player's prize also literally describes the bridegroom, the man of a marriage, or match.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a sporting accolade, while a wedding is a match whose principal male is the groom.

clue.text: Charm of fiesta can, somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters end up in some unspecified other arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tin can somehow captures the charm of a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: To fascinate is to enthral or captivate, which is to charm, both as verbs.

clue.text: Light ale brewed at that place inside

indicators.note: brewing mixes things up, so the drink's letters are stirred into a new order
inside puts the phrase about place within the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
there means at that place

explanation.surface: A pale beer has been brewed on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light ale' reads as a beer style; 'Light' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and airy, extremely light in weight or texture.

clue.text: The most tongue-tied manages this without the slightest exaggeration?

blocks.note: first meaning: a very tongue-tied person manages to utter the least of anyone
second meaning: the idiom for deliberate understatement

explanation.walkthrough: The first half takes the idiom literally: whoever is most lost for words speaks least.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom used when stating something mildly, signalling understatement rather than overstatement.

clue.text: Flowering plant in a Lancashire river

blocks.note: first meaning: a plant with flat clusters of small white flowers, also called milfoil
second meaning: a river flowing through Chorley in Lancashire, a county in north-west England

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a plant growing in a river; 'in' merely joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to a common wildflower, Achillea millefolium, and to a small river in north-west England.

clue.text: What one may have expected from 'Sweeney Todd' (musical affair)?

definitions.text: What one may have expected from 'Sweeney Todd'

blocks.note: Hair is a famous rock musical
a do is a party or affair

explanation.surface: A note on what audiences expect from the musical Sweeney Todd.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is itself a musical, which makes 'musical affair' look like a description of it; but Todd is a barber, so his customers would expect a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is a styled haircut, the service a barber such as Sweeney Todd provides.

clue.text: Game the French boycotted is over

indicators.note: boycotted means shunned, so those letters are kept out of the word

blocks.note: lacrosse is a field game played with netted sticks
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture ends after the French team stays away.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the L and the E of 'le' from the game, leaving the letters between.
explanation.definitionFit: Across and over are synonyms as prepositions, as in going across or over a bridge.

clue.text: Royal attendant has no time for messenger

indicators.note: has no means lacking, so one letter is taken away

blocks.note: a courtier attends a monarch at court
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A busy palace attendant has no time to act as a messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier carries parcels or messages, so is a messenger.

clue.text: Urge simple changes involving uranium

indicators.note: changes says the word is altered, so its letters are rearranged
involving means including, so one more letter is taken inside

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A call for simple reforms to include nuclear fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Urge' looks like a verb urging changes, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a sudden urge or desire to act.

clue.text: Writer, for example, brought up in a London suburb

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a pen is something you write with
e.g. abbreviates for example

explanation.surface: An author, say, was raised in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Penge is a district of south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Penge is a residential area in the London Borough of Bromley, so it is a suburb of the capital.

clue.text: Love game, possibly last in series

indicators.note: possibly hints at one possible version among many, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: love is a score of nil, written O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A love game might decide the final match in a tennis series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love game' reads as a tennis term, a game won without the loser scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the last in a sequence.

clue.text: I must be protected by guns regulation

indicators.note: something protected by another is shielded inside it, so one piece goes within

blocks.note: ordnance is artillery, big guns
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists that they be guarded by armed men, as the rules say.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordnance (big guns) and ordinance (a rule) differ by just the one letter, which is what the clue exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative rule or decree, a regulation.

clue.text: I may pose a problem for a dog

blocks.note: first meaning: the compiler of this puzzle, speaking as I, sets puzzling problems
second meaning: a breed of gun dog, such as the Irish red one

explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the crossword compiler speaking; the surface sounds like someone troubling a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A compiler sets clues and so is called by that title, and the same word names a long-haired hunting breed.

clue.text: Stand by wife, a sly type

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: A man who stands by his wife turns out to be shifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means beside, so W sits next to the stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is figuratively a sneaky, untrustworthy person.
